title: Metarhizium anisopliae Metabolites as Candidate Binders of Holotrichia oblita GH18 Chitinase: Binding Dynamics and Distal Cavity Remodeling
content: Entomopathogenic fungi produce chemically diverse metabolites whose insect molecular targets are often unresolved. We screened a literature-curated set of 42 reported Metarhizium anisopliae metabolites against a GH18 chitinase from the white grub Holotrichia oblita and reassessed the leading candidate by repeat docking and comparative molecular dynamics. Nineteen metabolites produced more favorable AutoDock Vina scores than historical Allosamidin, with Cytochalasin C (CYC) ranking first (−10.1 kcal mol⁻¹) and showing reproducible repeat-docking scores (−9.57 ± 0.06 kcal mol⁻¹). One 100-ns production trajectory was analyzed for apo, CYC-bound, and Allosamidin-bound chitinase. All systems underwent domain-scale rearrangement while retaining a comparatively stable catalytic core. CYC underwent a late binding-state transition, whereas Allosamidin retained an Asp739-centered anchor and a more favorable MM/GBSA binding-energy estimate (−34.23 ± 5.80 versus −21.82 ± 3.61 kcal mol⁻¹). A distal C2 cavity showed 66.0% broad occupancy in apo chitinase but 100% and 97.2% occupancy in CYC and Allosamidin trajectories, respectively. The results prioritize CYC as a candidate binder and support ligand-responsive distal cavity remodeling without establishing experimental inhibition or functional allostery.
